themes: VAM went from ~US$840/t (Q4FY26) to ~US$1,800-2,000/t at the peak; Pidilite consumed it at US$1,370/t in Q1FY27. By August it was ~50% off the peak (PL). Pidilite raised prices 2-12% by category and expects to pass some back as rebates.
MD (May-2026): 'buoyancy in urban demand' after GST 2.0 cuts and the income-tax relief; 'demand is holding quite well' (Aug-2026).
Penetration of tile adhesives and waterproofing
Tile & stone solutions market ~Rs 6,500 cr with 20-30% penetration (most tiles still fixed with cement); waterproofing back to 'mid-teens plus' growth for Pidilite in FY26-27.
A South Indian cement maker and tile makers entering tile adhesives; the largest paint company has built its own VAM/VAE plant; paint majors push waterproofing.
B2B export UVG −28.8% (Q3FY26), −21.8% (Q4FY26), −8.4% (Q1FY27); pigments are the main export line.
Rural/rurban growth ahead of urban for years (company); CRISIL flags weather risk to rural demand. June-September 2026 rain ended ~12.6% below normal (IMD).
MD: unorganised players 'struggle a little bit' in volatile input markets; 'too early' to see share gains.

moat: Brands (Fevicol, Dr. Fixit, M-Seal, Fevikwik, Araldite)
Fevicol 'synonymous with adhesives' (CRISIL); 12-15% price rises on Fevicol in Apr-May 2026 with C&B UVG still 12.2% in Q1FY27; competitors follow Pidilite's price moves 'almost to a T' (MD).
Real pricing power in the core.
5,700+ distributors, ~3.8 lakh dealers in Emerging India, 40,000+ rurban towns, 24,000+ Pidilite ki Duniya outlets, 1,700+ Dr. Fixit centres; carpenter, plumber and applicator programmes.
No captive VAM: Pidilite buys at market and 'rides the crests and troughs'; the largest paint company has built a VAM/VAE plant. Margins fell to 17-19% in FY22-23 when input costs spiked.
Margins swing with VAM; the moat protects share, not the margin in a spike.
Pidilite says it grows fastest in tile adhesives (top 4-5 players hold 80-90%); new entrants from cement and tiles; paint majors in waterproofing.
CRISIL calls it a 'bulk commodity business'; segment EBITDA margin 10-21% and export-dependent.
R&D ~Rs 115 cr (0.8% of revenue); technology partners Jowat, Litokol, Grupo Puma, ICA; new products (X-PER, M-Seal Advanced).
Steady renewal of the core rather than breakthrough IP.
